sents.t: It is Friday night.
Carlos and Emma are at my apartment.
We want pizza and a movie.
“Sam, you call the pizza place,” Emma says.
“It is good practice!”
I am a little nervous.
Talking on the phone in English is hard for me, because I can’t see the person’s face.
But I call Tony’s Pizza.
“Hi, Tony’s Pizza. Is this for pickup or delivery?”
“Um, delivery, please. Two large pizzas: one cheese pizza and one with mushrooms and peppers. And three bottles of soda.”
“OK. What’s your address and phone number?”
“14 Maple Street, Apartment 3. My number is 555-274-8190.”
“Thank you. That’s thirty-four dollars. It’s about forty minutes.”
Emma and Carlos clap.
“Perfect, Sam!”
Forty-five minutes later, the doorbell rings.
The pizza is hot and delicious.
We give the delivery driver a five-dollar tip.
“Thanks! Enjoy your pizza!” he says.
Now phone calls are not so scary for me.
